Re: Medical Necessity Appeal — Reduction Mammaplasty (Breast Reduction)
CPT Code(s): {{cpt_codes}}
ICD-10 Code(s): {{icd_codes}}

Dear Medical Director / Utilization Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for reduction mammaplasty for my patient. This procedure is medically necessary and is supported by the American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline for Reduction Mammaplasty (2011), CMS LCD L35041, and the Schnur Scale objective criteria.

CLINICAL ASSESSMENT SUMMARY:
Our Clinical Compass Breast Reduction Decision Support tool assessed this patient as: [Recommendation]
Schnur Scale Category: [Schnur Category]
Conservative Treatment Requirement Met: Pending — see documentation below



CLINICAL INDICATION:
This patient presents with macromastia (ICD-10: N62) causing significant functional impairment. The patient's breast size is disproportionate to her body habitus and has resulted in the following documented functional symptoms:

• Back pain (ICD-10: M54.5): [DESCRIBE — location, severity, duration, impact on function]
• Neck pain (ICD-10: M54.2): [DESCRIBE — location, severity, duration]
• Shoulder pain: [DESCRIBE — bilateral/unilateral, severity, duration]
• Bra strap shoulder grooving: [DESCRIBE — depth, pain, skin changes]
• Inframammary intertrigo: [DESCRIBE — rash, skin breakdown, treatment required]
• Postural problems: [DESCRIBE — kyphosis, forward head posture]
• [ADD ADDITIONAL SYMPTOMS AS APPLICABLE]

These symptoms have been present for [DURATION] and have significantly impaired the patient's ability to [DESCRIBE FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS: work, exercise, perform activities of daily living].

SCHNUR SCALE OBJECTIVE CRITERIA:
• Patient height: [HEIGHT] inches | Weight: [WEIGHT] lbs
• Body Surface Area (BSA): [BSA] m²
• Schnur Scale minimum resection weight for this BSA: [SCHNUR_MIN] grams per breast
• Estimated resection weight (surgeon estimate): [RESECTION_WEIGHT] grams per breast
• Schnur Scale criterion: [MET / NOT MET — if not met, emphasize functional symptoms]

The Schnur Scale (Schnur PL, et al., Plast Reconstr Surg 1997;100:875-883) is the standard objective criterion used by CMS LCD L35041 and most commercial payers to determine medical necessity for reduction mammaplasty.

CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT DOCUMENTATION:
The patient has undergone the following conservative treatments without adequate relief:

1. Physical Therapy: [DURATION] months of physical therapy with [PROVIDER], focusing on [DESCRIBE: postural strengthening, cervical/thoracic spine, shoulder girdle]. Outcome: [DESCRIBE — minimal/no improvement in back/neck/shoulder pain].

2. Supportive Bra / Minimizer Bra: Patient has worn [DESCRIBE] supportive bra. Outcome: [DESCRIBE — shoulder grooving persists, pain not adequately controlled].

3. NSAIDs / Medications: [DESCRIBE medications tried, duration, outcome].

4. Weight Loss: [DESCRIBE weight loss attempts, if applicable]. [Note: weight loss does not predictably reduce breast size in macromastia.]

Despite these conservative measures, the patient continues to experience [DESCRIBE ONGOING SYMPTOMS] that significantly impair her quality of life and functional capacity.

EVIDENCE-BASED JUSTIFICATION:

1. ASPS CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINE:
Per the ASPS Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline for Reduction Mammaplasty (2011), reduction mammaplasty is medically necessary when macromastia causes functional symptoms (back pain, shoulder pain, intertrigo, postural problems) that have not responded to conservative treatment. The guideline supports surgery as the definitive treatment for symptomatic macromastia.

2. SCHNUR SCALE AND CMS LCD L35041:
CMS LCD L35041 establishes that reduction mammaplasty is covered when: (1) the patient has macromastia with functional symptoms, (2) the estimated resection weight meets the Schnur Scale minimum for the patient's BSA, and (3) conservative treatment has been attempted. This patient [MEETS / BORDERLINE MEETS] the Schnur Scale criterion and has documented functional symptoms and conservative treatment failure.

3. OUTCOMES EVIDENCE:
Kerrigan et al. (Med Decis Making 2002;22:208-217) demonstrated significant improvement in functional symptoms, quality of life, and physical capacity following reduction mammaplasty. Saariniemi et al. (J Plast Surg Hand Surg 2014;48:239-244) confirmed significant improvement in pain, posture, and quality of life. Denial of this procedure will result in continued functional impairment and progressive musculoskeletal deterioration.
